SITAR growth curves and the pubertal growth spurt

Source: vignettes/growth-curves.Rmd
growth-curves.Rmd

About this vignette. All data are simulated with wgh_simulate(). The results show how the methods work and resemble the published patterns, but they are not the published findings and are not research results. SITAR models use at most 1,000 children each (development mode), the APHV bootstrap uses 10 replicates and the quantile bootstraps 50.

The pubertal growth spurt has a timing (age at peak height velocity, APHV), an intensity (peak height velocity, PHV) and a duration. This vignette shows how to estimate all three from school visits with SITAR models, and how to relate them to prepubertal BMI. It reproduces the analyses of three studies: the pubertal spurt by SITAR (Ho et al. 2026) [1], the distribution of pubertal growth velocity (Ho 2026) [2] and the duration of the spurt (Ho 2026) [3]. The vignette is precomputed because SITAR models take minutes to fit.

library(WeGrowHealthR)
wgh_config("dev")     # SITAR on up to 1,000 children per model, few bootstrap replicates
#> WeGrowHealthR run mode: dev
v <- wgh_simulate(30000, seed = 2026)$visits

1. Is there enough data at each age?

Mean curves are unreliable where few children are measured. wgh_age_density() counts children and visits in half-year bins and reports the age at which the number of children falls below 10% of its peak (share). The package trims velocity curves at that age.

ad <- wgh_age_density(v[v$age >= 6, ])
attr(ad, "sparse_from")
#> Female   Male 
#>   18.5   18.5

2. Fitting a SITAR model

SITAR (SuperImposition by Translation And Rotation) describes every child’s height curve as one mean curve shifted in size (a, cm), timing (b, years, negative means earlier) and intensity (c, on the log scale, positive means a faster, more intense spurt). wgh_fit_sitar() wraps sitar::sitar():

  • df is the flexibility of the mean spline (4 or 5 is usual),
  • fixed and random choose the effects ("a + b + c", or "a + b + c + d" for the extended model),
  • age_range the ages used and min_visits the visits needed per child,
  • max_children limits the number of children (set by the run mode).

It never stops on a failed fit. Instead it keeps the error, so competing models can be compared, and it retries once with one fewer degree of freedom.

boys <- v[v$sex == "Male" & v$age >= 6 & v$age <= 18, ]
fit_m <- wgh_fit_sitar(boys, df = 5, age_range = c(6, 18))
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 3643 children (run mode "dev").
fit_m
#> <wgh_sitar> "6-18 a+b+c": 3990 visits from 1000 children, df = 5
#> Population APHV 12.03 y, PHV 10.12 cm/y
#> # A tibble: 1 x 15
#>   model    converged n_children    AIC    BIC sigma  RMSE  sd_a  sd_b   sd_c  sd_d min_velocity_tail
#>   <chr>    <lgl>          <int>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>             <dbl>
#> 1 6-18 a+~ TRUE            1000 14992. 15087. 0.527 0.360  4.47 0.464 0.0715    NA             0.146
#> # i 3 more variables: max_re_corr <dbl>, APHV <dbl>, PHV <dbl>

The printout shows the number of children and visits, the population APHV and PHV, and diagnostics: whether the fit converged, whether the velocity curve turns negative in the tails, and the residual SD.

plot(fit_m, type = "both", line_width = 1.2)

plot() takes type = "velocity", "height" or "both", trim and show_data, plus the shared display options.

Checking the model

Two checks matter before using the estimates. wgh_check_identifiable() flags random effects that are almost perfectly correlated, a sign that the model cannot separate them. wgh_sitar_select() compares candidate specifications by BIC, a positive velocity in the tails and stable APHV and PHV, and picks one by a stated rule (the procedure used for girls in [1]).

wgh_check_identifiable(fit_m)
#> $ok
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $max_abs_corr
#> [1] 0.4927345
#> 
#> $pair
#> [1] "c-b"
#> 
#> $reason
#> [1] "OK: random effects c-b correlated at r = -0.493"
girls <- v[v$sex == "Female" & v$age >= 6 & v$age <= 16, ]
sel <- wgh_sitar_select(girls)
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 2938 children (run mode "dev").
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 2757 children (run mode "dev").
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 2938 children (run mode "dev").
sel$table
#> # A tibble: 3 x 21
#>   model converged n_children    AIC    BIC  sigma   RMSE  sd_a   sd_b   sd_c   sd_d
#>   <chr> <lgl>          <int>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 F1    TRUE            1000 15457. 15545.  0.519  0.339  5.23  0.763  0.103 NA    
#> 2 F2    FALSE             NA    NA     NA  NA     NA     NA    NA     NA     NA    
#> 3 F3    TRUE            1000 15428. 15548.  0.505  4.19   7.08  1.35   0.144  0.494
#> # i 10 more variables: min_velocity_tail <dbl>, max_re_corr <dbl>, APHV <dbl>, PHV <dbl>,
#> #   identifiable <lgl>, plausible_tail <lgl>, good_fit <lgl>, acceptable <lgl>, why_not <chr>,
#> #   stable <lgl>
sel$selected
#> [1] "F1"
sel$reason
#> [1] "No candidate met all criteria (F1: velocity falls below the tolerance in the tail; F2: did not converge; F3: residual error more than twice the best model). The first model is kept and its mean curve should be displayed only within the age range with adequate data."
fit_f <- sel$fits[[sel$selected]]

Read sel$reason before using the selected model. Here, with a subsample of 1,000 girls in development mode, no candidate meets every criterion, so the function keeps the first model and says why each candidate failed. With the full cohort (wgh_config("publication")) more candidates may converge. When none is acceptable, show the mean curve only over the ages with enough data and report the reason with the results.

3. APHV and PHV with honest intervals

wgh_aphv() gives the population APHV and PHV from the mean curve. wgh_sitar_ci() adds intervals. The default method = "bootstrap" resamples children and refits the model B times, which carries all the uncertainty of the curve. method = "legacy" reproduces the interval of the original analysis code (the estimate plus or minus 1.96 times the SD of individual APHV over the square root of n). It is not a bootstrap: it treats the spread of individual timing as sampling error, so its width has no clear meaning, and it is kept only to match published numbers.

ci_m <- wgh_sitar_ci(fit_m, B = 10)
ci_m
#> # A tibble: 1 x 9
#>   method             aphv aphv_lower aphv_upper   phv phv_lower phv_upper n_children replicates
#>   <chr>             <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>      <int>      <int>
#> 1 cluster bootstrap  12.0       12.0       12.1  10.1      10.0      10.2       1000         10
wgh_sitar_ci(fit_m, method = "legacy")
#> # A tibble: 1 x 9
#>   method                  aphv aphv_lower aphv_upper   phv phv_lower phv_upper n_children replicates
#>   <chr>                  <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>      <int>      <int>
#> 1 legacy (not a bootstr~  12.0       12.0       12.1  10.1      10.1      10.2       1000         NA

With 1,000 children the population curve is estimated precisely, so both intervals are narrow here. With B = 10 the bootstrap interval is rough. Use B = 200 or more for a paper (wgh_config("publication") does that).

4. Individual timing and intensity

wgh_sitar_effects() returns one row per child with the random effects and the child’s own APHV and PHV. The individual APHV uses the exact SITAR formula, not an approximation. early_timing flags children whose timing is earlier than the population (b < early_cut), and faster_tempo children with a more intense spurt (c > 0).

eff_m <- wgh_sitar_effects(fit_m)
eff_f <- wgh_sitar_effects(fit_f)
head(eff_m)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 10
#>   id           a       b       c  aphv   phv early_timing faster_tempo aphv_population sex  
#>   <chr>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <lgl>        <lgl>                  <dbl> <fct>
#> 1 C000026  4.03  -0.181   0.0765  11.8 10.9  TRUE         TRUE                    12.0 Male 
#> 2 C000036 -0.773  0.183  -0.0597  12.3  9.53 FALSE        FALSE                   12.0 Male 
#> 3 C000044  2.16  -0.286   0.0900  11.6 11.1  TRUE         TRUE                    12.0 Male 
#> 4 C000049  5.20  -0.395   0.0615  11.6 10.8  TRUE         TRUE                    12.0 Male 
#> 5 C000118 -0.985 -0.671   0.0391  11.3 10.5  TRUE         TRUE                    12.0 Male 
#> 6 C000143 -2.93   0.0406  0.0449  12.0 10.6  FALSE        TRUE                    12.0 Male
summary(eff_m$aphv)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   10.45   11.78   12.03   12.03   12.30   13.53
summary(eff_f$aphv)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   7.346   8.492   9.046   9.104   9.634  11.710

Girls reach their peak years before boys, the most consistent finding of growth studies, and individual APHV varies around the population value, more in girls than in boys.

Next step. Join these effects to other data by id, for example to ask whether prepubertal BMI predicts earlier timing (section 7).

5. Velocity curves of individual children

wgh_velocity_panel() evaluates each child’s velocity curve on a grid, either by age (time = "age") or by years from the child’s own APHV (time = "aphv"). observed_only = TRUE keeps only the part of each curve covered by the child’s visits, so no child is extrapolated.

pan <- wgh_velocity_panel(fit_m, time = "aphv", grid = seq(-4, 4, by = 0.05), observed_only = FALSE)
head(pan)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   id        age  time height velocity
#>   <chr>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 C000026  7.76 -4      130.     5.71
#> 2 C000026  7.81 -3.95   130.     5.70
#> 3 C000026  7.86 -3.9    131.     5.68
#> 4 C000026  7.91 -3.85   131.     5.66
#> 5 C000026  7.96 -3.8    131.     5.65
#> 6 C000026  8.01 -3.75   131.     5.63

6. Duration of the spurt

wgh_curve_features() measures the width of each child’s velocity peak. The default (reference = "takeoff") measures the width at 25%, 50% and 75% of the spurt amplitude, that is, the rise from the take-off velocity to the peak. Older code measured the width at a fraction of PHV (reference = "zero"), but the velocity of most children never falls to half of PHV before the data start, so that width is left-censored for most of them. The package reports censoring so this cannot go unnoticed.

cf <- wgh_curve_features(pan)
summary(cf$width_p50)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   1.883   2.218   2.303   2.308   2.393   2.811
pan_f <- wgh_velocity_panel(fit_f, time = "aphv", grid = seq(-4, 4, by = 0.05), observed_only = FALSE)
censored <- function(p) c(amplitude = mean(wgh_curve_features(p)$censored_left_p50),
  fraction_of_phv = mean(wgh_curve_features(p, thresholds = 0.5, reference = "zero")$censored_left_p50))
rbind(boys = censored(pan), girls = censored(pan_f))
#>       amplitude fraction_of_phv
#> boys          0               0
#> girls         0               1

width_p50 is the width of the spurt in years at half its amplitude. The second table gives the share of children whose width cannot be measured because the velocity curve does not fall far enough before the data start. Girls start their spurt early, so with the legacy definition the width is censored for most of them, while the amplitude definition measures every child.

7. Does prepubertal BMI change the spurt?

The prepubertal exposure is the earliest BAZ from 5 years at or before 11 years in boys and 9 years in girls (see vignette("trajectories")).

base <- wgh_index_exposure(v, "baz", name = "pre")
base <- base[!duplicated(base$id), c("id", "pre_value")]
names(base)[2] <- "baz_pre"
e <- merge(eff_m, base, by = "id")
summary(lm(b ~ baz_pre, data = e))$coefficients
#>                Estimate  Std. Error    t value     Pr(>|t|)
#> (Intercept)  0.09209288 0.015171065   6.070298 1.937841e-09
#> baz_pre     -0.10053821 0.008473308 -11.865285 4.094392e-30

A negative slope means higher prepubertal BMI goes with earlier timing.

The second study asked whether the association is the same across the distribution. wgh_scalar_quantiles() fits quantile regressions of a child-level outcome with a bootstrap over children, and reports the OLS estimate alongside:

wgh_scalar_quantiles(e, b ~ baz_pre, "baz_pre", taus = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9), B = 50)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 5
#>   model        tau estimate   lower   upper
#>   <chr>      <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 quantile    0.1   -0.110  -0.138  -0.0870
#> 2 quantile    0.25  -0.108  -0.133  -0.0890
#> 3 quantile    0.5   -0.0883 -0.116  -0.0701
#> 4 quantile    0.75  -0.0860 -0.0988 -0.0557
#> 5 quantile    0.9   -0.0764 -0.112  -0.0625
#> 6 OLS (mean) NA     -0.101  -0.117  -0.0839

wgh_mediation() asks how much of the association of BMI with PHV passes through earlier timing:

wgh_mediation(e, "baz_pre", "b", "phv", B = 50)
#> # A tibble: 4 x 4
#>   effect                  estimate   lower  upper
#>   <chr>                      <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 Total effect             0.108    0.0828 0.149 
#> 2 Natural direct effect   -0.00492 -0.0216 0.0348
#> 3 Natural indirect effect  0.113    0.0910 0.141 
#> 4 Proportion mediated      1.05     0.763  1.23

The total effect is the change in PHV per unit of prepubertal BAZ. The natural indirect effect is the part that passes through timing b, and the natural direct effect the rest. A proportion mediated near or slightly above 1 means that essentially all of the association works through earlier timing (a proportion above 1 occurs when the direct effect is slightly negative).

8. The three studies in one call each

wgh_flow_pubertal_spurt() runs the age-density check, the male model, the female model selection, identifiability checks, APHV and PHV with intervals, individual effects and the links between prepubertal anthropometry and timing. Its report is then passed as spurt to the velocity and duration flows, so the SITAR models are fitted only once.

spurt <- wgh_flow_pubertal_spurt(v)
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 3643 children (run mode "dev").
#> SITAR fitted to a random 1000 of 2938 children (run mode "dev").
spurt
#> 
#> -- Pubertal growth spurt by SITAR (Ho et al. 2026, medRxiv 2026.07.26.26358986) --
#> 
#> Tables (7): age_density, model_diagnostics, aphv_phv_population, individual_effects,
#> individual_summary, timing_models, early_timing_logistic
#> Figures (3): fig_velocity, fig_height, fig_aphv_by_bmi
#> Models: sitar_male, sitar_female
#> Diagnostics: identifiability
#> Settings: mode = dev; ci_B = 0
spurt$tables$aphv_phv_population
#> # A tibble: 2 x 10
#>   sex    method           aphv aphv_lower aphv_upper   phv phv_lower phv_upper n_children replicates
#>   <chr>  <chr>           <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>      <int>      <int>
#> 1 Male   legacy (not a ~  12.0      12.0       12.1  10.1      10.1      10.2        1000         NA
#> 2 Female legacy (not a ~   9.1       9.06       9.14  7.93      7.89      7.98       1000         NA
spurt$tables$early_timing_logistic
#> # A tibble: 4 x 7
#>   sex    term    odds_ratio lower upper  p_value   auc
#>   <chr>  <chr>        <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Female baz_pre       1.29  1.13  1.47 1.48e- 4 0.631
#> 2 Female haz_pre       1.30  1.05  1.61 1.50e- 2 0.631
#> 3 Male   baz_pre       1.51  1.35  1.70 2.65e-12 0.781
#> 4 Male   haz_pre       2.98  2.41  3.68 3.36e-24 0.781
plot(spurt, "fig_velocity")

plot(spurt, "fig_aphv_by_bmi")

velocity <- wgh_flow_velocity_distribution(v, spurt = spurt)
velocity$tables$scalar_quantiles
#> # A tibble: 36 x 7

duration <- wgh_flow_spurt_duration(v, spurt = spurt)

plot(velocity, "fig_velocity_slopes")

Where to go next

  • The individual SITAR effects are features for prediction (vignette("prediction")) and growth phenotypes (vignette("phenotypes-states")). Size a is estimated from the late visits, so it must not be used to predict late height. The package never joins it.
  • wgh_fpca_curves() decomposes the velocity curves into their main shapes.

References

  1. Ho NT, Nguyen QV, Dao AQ, Tran CTL, Pham AN. Pubertal growth spurt characteristics of Vietnamese urban schoolchildren: population and individual level analysis using SITAR. medRxiv. 2026. 2026.07.26.26358986. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.26.26358986

  2. Ho NT. Prepubertal body mass index reshapes the distribution of pubertal growth velocity in Vietnamese children: a SITAR-based quantile analysis. medRxiv. 2026. 2026.09.04.26362313. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.04.26362313

  3. Ho NT. Body mass index and the duration of the pubertal growth spurt in Vietnamese urban children. medRxiv. 2026. 2026.09.09.26362696. https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.09.26362696
